column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The towns are called your gates in the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “which I have not commanded,” rather than explicitly saying “forbidden.”
The Hebrew explicitly says “behold” and describes the matter as established.
The Hebrew repeats the man or woman, then uses plural pronouns for stoning them and says separately that they shall die.
The Hebrew twice describes testimony as the mouth of the witness or witnesses.
The hand of the witnesses and the hand of all the people are each singular in the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the paired terms: between blood and blood, between case and case, and between blow and blow.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the word is reported from that place.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says that man shall die, rather than explicitly using a passive verb of execution.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “I will set a king over me,” with singular address throughout the quoted resolve.
The Hebrew continues to address one person and emphasizes appointing the king.
The Hebrew does not explicitly repeat the noun king and retains the plural addressees in the LORD’s quoted command.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the copy is to be from before the Levitical priests.
The Hebrew separately joins keeping the words and statutes and doing them.
The Hebrew calls his countrymen his brothers and describes prolonged rule as lengthening days.
